consistency_check_details.description: The August 2025 lower bound of over 45,000 admissions and the undated website count of 50,000 are preserved as differently scoped observations.
Patient, admission, and image counts are explicitly distinguished, preventing false cross-source discrepancies.
Prospective sampling, annotation, deidentification, EEG extraction, and holdout descriptions are not asserted as completed released-data features.
The NIH funding entry contains grant details and aligns with the stated critical-care data-generation purposes.
The public-availability goal, current controlled access, program-specific agreement, and repository MIT license are differentiated rather than treated as equivalent permissions.
The stated project start and end dates are logically ordered and encompass the dated 2025 documentation.
The deidentification field contains no established released-data status or method, and participant privacy protections are not comprehensively documented.
Training-program access and licensing documentation cannot establish permissions or governance for other users.
Missing collection periods, processing dates, and release identifiers prevent a complete collection-to-release temporal consistency check.

semantic_insights: The record distinguishes released observations from future plans for cohort size, sampling, annotation, deidentification, EEG extraction, and holdout validation.
Counts preserve their units: admissions, patients, images, radiology-associated admissions, EHR rows, and waveform volume are not silently equated.
Funding attribution is detailed and internally aligned with the documented critical-care AI purposes.
Named standards and semantic-mapping resources provide substantive interoperability evidence without relying solely on an AI-ready label.
The record explicitly prevents the GitHub project's MIT license from being misrepresented as the dataset license.
The principal deductions reflect missing documentation, not demonstrated absence of real-world safeguards or proven contradictions in the dataset.
